title: Orsen and the Sigil
premise: Tamsin Eastwick's beast-speaker gift is a death sentence in Vellmark, where the Sigil-law bans all magic, so she has survived a decade by hiding it behind harmless charms. When the border wards collapse and the stars vanish, she learns the covenant her grandmother helped forge between the human city and the wild realm of Orsen was deliberately broken — and that the wardens who did it are hunting everyone with old blood, including her. Guided by a wounded griffin and the exiled heir of Orsen, Tamsin must reach the Heartstone and reforge the covenant before the realms bleed into each other. She succeeds only by refusing the warden's offer to seize the covenant's power for herself, binding it instead to a new found family sworn across both worlds.
about_author: Rosalind Ashgrove is the pen name of a former wildlife rehabilitator who spent years listening to animals she could never answer. She writes fantasy about the conversations we wish we could have, from a farmhouse full of rescued creatures.

chapters.title: The Night the Stars Went Out
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Selling charms in the market city of Vellmark, Tamsin hides her gift even from her found-family of fellow charm-sellers. That night the stars vanish, the border wards shatter, and a dying griffin crashes into her shop speaking her name in her grandmother's voice. The beat: terror giving way to reluctant responsibility as she chooses to flee with the creature rather than report it.

chapters.title: What the Wardens Buried
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, with interludes from warden-captain Serl's cold perspective. Crossing into the darkened wilds, Tamsin meets Kaelen, exiled heir of Orsen, and learns the covenant was broken deliberately to hoard its power. Serl's hunters close in, killing a friend from her old life. The beat: grief hardening into purpose, and the first flicker of trust between Tamsin and Kaelen.

chapters.title: The Heartstone's Price
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At the ruined Heartstone, Serl offers Tamsin everything: legitimacy, safety, and the covenant's power bound to her alone — all she must do is claim it and let the wild realm die. The griffin sacrifices itself buying time, and Tamsin nearly accepts, feeling the corruption of easy power. The beat: the climax, where she refuses, and the reforging begins through shared blood and sworn names.

chapters.title: A Covenant of Small Voices
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, closing with Kaelen's. The covenant rekindled, stars return over a healing border, but Serl escapes with a splinter of stolen power — a seed for what comes next. Tamsin, no longer hiding, opens a school for gifted children with Kaelen and her chosen family. The beat: quiet resolution; inheritance transformed from burden into belonging.
